title: Exposed dashboards and APIs require authentication
summary: Any remotely exposed dashboard, API or webhook surface authenticates callers and rejects anonymous access.

protected.asset: Gateway-adjacent control surfaces reachable from the network
protected.failure: An unauthenticated stranger reaches the dashboard, API or webhook and drives the deployment or reads its state.

rationale: Public exposure turns every service surface into an Internet-reachable door. Anonymous rejection, exact-origin checks and signature or replay protections must match the exposure actually observed from an authorized external vantage point, not the bind address alone.

variants.description: Use the service's own authentication and pairing surfaces; verify anonymous requests are rejected from an external vantage point.
Terminate an authenticating reverse proxy in front of the service with loopback-only upstream binds.

verification.method: From an authorized external vantage point, request each exposed surface without credentials and with wrong credentials; all must be rejected, and published container ports must be verified bound as intended, remembering published ports bypass host firewalls.
verification.evidence: Rejection outcomes per surface and vantage point, plus bind and publish inventory; no tokens or session values.

rollback.method: Restore the previous listener and proxy configuration; confirm the owner's access path survives before declaring rollback complete.

failure_modes: A dashboard is bound to loopback in-container but published on all host interfaces.
Auth protects the browser path while the API path allows anonymous calls.
A proxy layer is added without removing a still-reachable direct bind.

hermes_versions.notes: Synthetic seed control: the range is an illustrative placeholder for the example registry, not a verified compatibility claim.
